name: ESCAPADE
tagline: Twin Blue and Gold orbiters bound for Mars to study its magnetosphere from two places at once
description: ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) is NASA's pair of identical Mars orbiters, Blue and Gold, built by Rocket Lab. The Space Sciences Laboratory at UC Berkeley leads the mission, Robert Lillis is its principal investigator, and it is part of NASA's SIMPLEx program. Each spacecraft has a dry mass of 209 kg and a fuelled mass of 535 kg. They launched together on Blue Origin's New Glenn, flight NG-2, from Cape Canaveral on 2025-11-13, then looped around the Sun-Earth Lagrange point L2 in a loiter orbit until Earth and Mars were aligned. On 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-09 the two spacecraft made powered Earth flybys, two days apart, the first time NASA has used one to head for Mars, and both are now on a 10-month cruise, with orbit insertion planned for 2027-09-07 and 2027-09-09. Science is expected to begin in June 2028, measuring from two places at once how the solar wind drives atmospheric loss at Mars.
best_known_for: Twin orbiters sent to Mars after a loiter orbit, by NASA's first powered Earth flyby toward Mars
